title: Welcome to SA Multimedia Digest, where we combine videos and
text:
Welcome to SA Multimedia Digest, where we combine videos and podcasts from across Seeking Alpha's contributor base into a single weekly article.
After a few weeks spent on market swings and economic data releases, we're focusing today on a little-known company called Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ).
Andres Cardenal and Cheddar TV start things off with his bullish case: despite a decrease in demand for iPhones last quarter, Apple is still trading at reasonably low valuation and continues to have a lot of things going for it.

Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) announced that it will slash output of its OLED panels in response to reportedly weak demand for the iPhone 10. Is this something that investors should be concerned about, Andres?
Not really, I think investors need to focus on the big picture where you look at Apple on the big numbers, the company is making like $50 billion or maybe $60 billion in free cash flow, is trading for reasonably low valuation. So you have a company which is generating lots of money trading for a very reasonable valuation and is still generating high speed revenue growth.

Sven Carlin also took a look at Apple this week, focusing on long term strategy and why Buffett made it his largest portfolio holding.

Apple is one of the most discussed stocks out there so there is no point in going into a detailed analysis. Where I think I can add value is by discussing AAPL from a long term perspective, one many fail to see, and which could be the reason Buffett has made AAPL his largest portfolio holding.
If you go through AAPL's conference call you will see how almost all of the analysts covering the stock focus on short term issues like the iPhone cycle, the capital structure etc. They consequently insert what they see has changed into their models and estimate AAPL's target price.
However, I don't think Buffett is concerned whether the new HomePod will show stellar sales or not. He is more concerned about things like moats, return on invested capital, cash available to shareholders, the efficiency of buybacks and the capacity AAPL has to generate strong cash flows in the future. Of course, the strong current earnings and cash flows help but there is so much more to AAPL.
